findings.assertion: The December 1914 occupation by Villa and Zapata followed the December 4 Xochimilco agreement; the capital's food crisis must be explained alongside the competing armies' unstable political control, not presented as one uncontested Revolutionary government.
findings.source_locator: Muro PDF printed pp.2–3, footnote 2; Ávila 1991 journal abstract
findings.limitations: Treat Xochimilco pact and capital entry as distinct events; original military dispatches not inspected.

findings.assertion: The conventionalist authorities attempted food price controls and free grain relief; Muro describes 21 December 1914 ration distribution in Azcapotzalco using tickets for maize, wheat and beans, citing an El Monitor report dated 21 December.
findings.source_locator: Muro printed p.3 and fn.7 citing El Monitor 21 Dec 1914 p.3
findings.limitations: The 1914 newspaper itself was not opened; exact plaza, queue dimensions and food quantities unverified.

findings.assertion: Control over acceptable paper money shifted between conventionists and constitutionalists in 1914–15; Muro describes Obregón's January 1915 rejection of conventionist notes, associated shop closures and heightened barriers to food purchases.
findings.source_locator: Muro printed p.4 and fn.13, discussion of 'coloraditos' and 'dos caritas'
findings.limitations: The dates and enforceability of individual monetary orders require original decrees; causation not reduced to currency alone.

findings.assertion: Food shortages during the 1915 crisis were attributed by Muro to damaged or militarily diverted rail transport, interruptions in regional supplies and speculation, with wartime migration increasing demand; this is a multifactor explanation, not a single-cause drought narrative.
geographies: Mexico City and regional rail corridors
findings.source_locator: Muro printed pp.3–5; Martínez Ocampo UNAM doctoral thesis repository metadata identifies 1913–17 abasto/subsistence scope
findings.limitations: Doctoral thesis full chapters and freight ledgers not inspected; do not quantify relative contributions.

findings.assertion: The 1915–1916 typhus epidemic overlapped the food crisis; Molina del Villar attributes the city's vulnerability in part to poverty, disrupted sanitation spending, war and changing administrations, based on archival, press and public-health documentation.
findings.source_locator: Molina del Villar 2015 institutional abstract, pp.1163–1247 full article uninspected; Muro PDF printed p.5
findings.limitations: Epidemic case counts, mortality and neighborhood comparisons not yet validated against original tables.

findings.assertion: Muro reports demonstrations beginning in popular streets or areas around La Merced, Capuchinas and Uruguay, where residents challenged food shortages and invalid currency, before petitioning Obregón's headquarters.
geographies: La Merced / Capuchinas / República de Uruguay
findings.source_locator: Muro printed p.6, footnote 17 citing Ramírez Plancarte p.367; page image visually checked
findings.limitations: No exact procession route, headquarters address or surviving building verified; on-site walk must not invent a route.

findings.assertion: Muro cites distribution of small-denomination constitutionalist notes by the Junta Revolucionaria de Auxilios al Pueblo at the Interoceanic railway station, in amounts of 5, 10, 15 and 20 pesos; station location needs historic-map corroboration before attaching modern coordinates.
themes: rail hub and emergency public relief
geographies: Former Interoceanic railway station, exact footprint unresolved
findings.source_locator: Muro printed p.6, footnote 18 citing Ramírez Plancarte pp.371–373; screenshot of p.6 inspected
findings.limitations: Original payment ledger and station map unavailable, and nominal pesos cannot be equated with purchasing power.

findings.assertion: For a Merced market-history walk, 1915 relief, shop closures and street protest must be connected to older nineteenth-century city market infrastructure rather than conflating present-day Mercado de la Merced with every historical 1915 market location.
findings.source_locator: Rosas Barrera abstract and AHCM market collections list lines 31–83; Muro printed pp.4–6
findings.limitations: No georeferenced 1915 market plans or specific shop inventory; modern market buildings require separate dating.

findings.assertion: INEHRM's 1915 dossier includes an INAH/SINAFO Casasola photograph of people queued for relief rations, captioned approximately 1915; it could illustrate civilian experience if the object ID, original caption/date and reproduction license are confirmed.
themes: historical photographic evidence of food relief
findings.source_locator: Muro printed p.1, Casasola SINAFO caption; photo object identity not verified independently
findings.limitations: Do not claim exact site, date, photographer or reproduction rights from a secondary caption.

findings.assertion: The 2016 INEHRM volume reports maize at 7.5 centavos/kg in December 1911 and 31 centavos/kg in June 1915 but labels this a 370% increase; those endpoints mathematically imply about a 313.3% increase (4.13-fold). Preserve this internal discrepancy for source correction.
themes: historical price statistics and measurement integrity
findings.source_locator: Felipe Arturo Ávila Espinosa, 2016, Contexto histórico, printed p.95, PDF text index
findings.limitations: The book's claimed 370% is inconsistent with stated endpoints; original market price series, units, and any rounding not checked. Do not publish either percentage as settled.

findings.assertion: Molina del Villar's separate 2018 analysis places constitutionalist children's asylum policy between 1915 and 1918 and describes shelter closures amid fiscal and sanitary difficulties, making it an evidence trail for assessing who bore the urban crisis's costs.
themes: child welfare institutional medicine and humanitarian relief
geographies: Mexico City, specific asylum locations unresolved
findings.source_locator: 2018 research summary identifies pp.195–242; 2015 epidemiology summary for adjacent sanitation context
findings.limitations: Archival asylum registers, institution addresses, population counts and causal details not yet inspected.
